conbody.p: When Impala compute nodes and its storage are not co-located, the network bandwidth requirement goes up as the network traffic includes the data fetch as well as the shuffling exchange traffic of intermediate results.
To mitigate the pressure on the network, you can enable the compute nodes to cache the working set read from remote filesystems, such as, remote HDFS data node, S3, ABFS, ADLS.

When block location loading is turned off for HDFS or Ozone, Impala schedules every scan range on them as a remote read, so the data cache can serve all reads from them. See Turning Off Block Location Loading.
To enable remote data cache, set the --data_cache Impala Daemon start-up flag as below:
The flag is set to a list of directories, separated by ,, followed by a :, and a capacity quota per directory.
If set to an empty string, data caching is disabled.
Cached data is stored in the specified directories.
The specified directories must exist in the local filesystem of each Impala Daemon, or Impala will fail to start.
In addition, the filesystem which the directory resides in must support hole punching.
The cache can consume up to the quota bytes for each of the directories specified.
The default setting for --data_cache is an empty string.
For example, with the following setting, the data cache may use up to 1 TB, with 500 GB max in /data/0 and /data/1 respectively.

In Impala 3.4 and higher, you can configure one of the following cache eviction policies for the data cache:
LRU (Least Recently Used--the default)
LIRS (Inter-reference Recency Set) LIRS is a scan-resistent, low performance-overhead policy. You configure a cache eviction policy using the --data_cache_eviction_policy Impala Daemon start-up flag:
conbody.note: The cache item will not expire as long as the same file metadata is used in the query. This is because the cache key consists of the filename, mtime (last modified time of the file), and file offset. If the mtime in the file metadata remains unchanged, the scan request will consistently access the cache (provided that there is enough capacity).

section.title: Consistent Scheduling of Remote Reads
section.p: To make file-related caches, such as the data cache, more efficient, Impala schedules the reads of each file split from a remote filesystem to a small, consistent set of executors. The NUM_REMOTE_EXECUTOR_CANDIDATES query option sets the size of the set, 3 by default. If the option is 0, the reads can be scheduled to any executor. Impala picks the executors by hashing the path and offset of the split onto a hash ring of the executors in the executor group. By default, the positions of an executor on the hash ring are derived from its IP address. Therefore, different executor groups schedule the same file split to unrelated executors, and the scheduling changes when the executors restart with different IP addresses.

Starting in , you can set the ‑‑scheduling_seed startup flag on each executor to derive its positions on the hash ring from the specified string instead of its IP address. The value must be unique among the executors of an executor group, but executors in different executor groups can use the same value. For example, in a cluster with several executor groups of 8 executors, the third executor of each group can use ‑‑scheduling_seed=executor_3_of_8, so that all the executor groups pick the executors with the same scheduling seeds for a given file split. The scheduling also stays the same when an executor restarts with a different IP address, but with the same scheduling seed. The default is an empty string, which means that the IP address of the executor is used.
